title: Sky-high Jamsil
theme: Chuseok day — stick to places confirmed open
summary: Lotte World Tower day: lake walk, French bistro lunch at the Sofitel, glass-floor observatory, then back near home for a hotel buffet and the Banpo rainbow fountain.

stops.note: Flat loop around the lake with the tower above you.
French bistro & boulangerie in the Sofitel, 5 min from the lake. Hotel restaurant — expected open on Chuseok; book ahead.
Buy tickets online the morning of. Glass-floor Sky Deck on 118F; 120F terrace.
Mall opens noon on Chuseok day. Browse or rest before heading home.
Dinner buffet near home — no transfers needed after.
Shows at 19:30, 20:00, 20:30, 21:00, 21:30 (20 min each). Cancelled in rain or strong wind.

legs.to: Banpo Hangang Park & Moonlight Rainbow Fountain

tips: Chuseok day: many small restaurants close — every stop here is confirmed open or a hotel/mall.
Nightcap option: MOBO Bar at JW Marriott is 15 min on foot from the fountain.
Want Korean fine dining instead? Bicena (81F, Lotte World Tower) is open 12:30 on Chuseok day.
Rather sit down? Lotte Cinema Super Plex G (one of Korea's biggest screens) is in the same mall — Hollywood films play in English with Korean subtitles (look for 자막).

legs.from: Banpo Hangang Park & Moonlight Rainbow Fountain

title: Downtown lights
theme: Chuseok holiday — modern downtown, no palaces
summary: Zaha Hadid's DDP, Seoul's most famous noodle lunch, Apple Myeongdong and the shopping lanes, sunset from N Seoul Tower, then Alabama BBQ and live jazz in Itaewon.

stops.note: Walk the silver curves and roof path for free; exhibitions inside are optional.
Seoul's most famous kalguksu (since 1966): noodles ₩12,000, dumplings ₩13,000. The queue moves fast.
Glass-and-light flagship — try the latest devices, no pressure to buy.
K-beauty flagships with instant tax refunds — bring passports.
Uphill — take a Venti/TADA or bus 01A/01B to the top, not the walk. Sunset ≈18:17; observatory ticket optional (≈₩29,000).
Taxi down from the tower (~11 min). Brisket and ribs platters to share; the Mega platter (₩129,000) + a side feeds five.
Korea's oldest jazz club, live bands nightly. Cover ₩15,000 per person per set; book a table for 5.

tips: From N Seoul Tower to Itaewon: bus down or a Venti/TADA van (~10 min).
Show option: NANTA (wordless kitchen-percussion comedy) is 3 min from the Myeongdong stop — check weekend showtimes on nanta.co.kr.
Splurge lunch instead: Gigas (Michelin-starred Mediterranean at Piknic) — tasting menus ₩220,000–290,000 per person; book ahead.

title: Yeouido & the river
summary: Brunch in Seorae Village, then Seoul’s most futuristic department store, Paris’s Centre Pompidou and the new 60th-floor sky deck, fried chicken on the riverbank, a balloon ride and a sunset cruise, and dinner 37 floors up at the Conrad.

stops.note: Calm all-day brunch kitchen 10 min from home. Early-bird set until 09:00, then the full menu.
do: Order: shakshuka-style eggs, tomato omelette (₩19,000), hummus plate (₩19,000), daily soup with toast (₩11,000)
Sleeping in? Skip it and eat at The Hyundai food hall instead

stops.note: Glass-roofed store with an indoor forest and waterfall. Arrive at opening, before the Sunday crowds.
do: 5F Sounds Forest: indoor garden under the glass roof, 12 m waterfall
B1/B2 pop-up halls: rotating brand exhibitions
12:00 lunch at the B1 food hall (Tasty Seoul): burgers, pasta, Korean, bakeries; ≈₩18k per person
IFC Mall (Zara, Uniqlo, Muji) is 3 min away underground if anyone wants more shops

stops.note: The Paris Pompidou’s new Seoul branch (opened June 2026). Show: “Cubist: Innovators of Vision”, with Picasso, Braque and Léger loans.
do: Book timed tickets online in the morning; Sunday afternoons sell out
Adults ₩28,000
Closes 18:00 today, closed Mondays

stops.note: Same building: the 60th-floor sky deck reopened in June 2026 with 360° river views.
do: Rooftop terrace on the old helipad: the best photo of the day
Starbucks on the deck: coffee break with a view
Ticket price not yet published; pay at the door

stops.note: Seoul’s favourite riverbank. Do chimaek (chicken + beer) on the grass, the most local thing you can do.
do: Buy a mat and cold beer at the GS25/CU by Yeouinaru Stn exit 2–3
Order fried chicken (BHC/Kyochon ≈₩23k each; two feed five) to the park’s delivery zone, or ask the shop staff to help
Try instant ramyeon from the river convenience-store machine

stops.note: Tethered balloon 130 m up; a 15-min ride. Cancelled in wind; check the queue screen at the park.
do: ≈₩22,000 each; buy tickets on site
Queue can be 20–30 min on Sundays; go before sunset

stops.note: Sunset sailing from Yeouinaru pier: 40 min past the 63 Building and Bamseom islets with the bridges lighting up.
do: Take the sailing nearest sunset, ≈18:00 (sunset ticket ₩22,900)
Sit on the upper open deck on the way out
Book on the E-Land Cruise site or buy at the pier kiosk

stops.note: Dinner and nightcap on the Conrad’s top floor: grill plates, 250+ whiskies and river views.
do: Ask for a window table when booking
Steaks and grill mains, then a whisky flight for the parents
Smart-casual; 10 min walk or ≈₩6k taxi from the pier
stops.book: Call Conrad Seoul or book via the hotel site

tips: Cheaper dinner: IFC Mall’s restaurant floor (L2–L3) has casual Western chains right next to the Conrad.
Splurge: Walking on the Cloud (Italian, 59F of the 63 Building): courses ₩195k–250k per person.
Order chicken in English: Coupang Eats and Baemin need a Korean phone number. Otherwise walk to a chicken shop near Yeouinaru Stn and carry it over.

title: Gangnam future
summary: Samsung’s hands-on tech flagship, the Starfield Library and the COEX WAVE screen, American pizza, Hyundai’s car-tech showroom, Gentle Monster’s robot art, an 80-minute massage, then a New York steakhouse and a world-ranked cocktail bar.

stops.note: Samsung’s biggest flagship: try the newest foldables, OLED gaming rigs and the media-art stairs.
do: Try the latest Galaxy Fold/Flip and the AI features on the ground floor
Walk up the tiered lounge: media-art installation
Tax refund on the spot with a passport; Korean phones may be region-locked

stops.note: The 13 m wall of bookshelves; best photos before lunchtime crowds.
do: Photo from the top of the central staircase
Free, no ticket

stops.note: Asia’s largest underground mall. Browse, then head out for lunch.
do: Kakao Friends and Line Friends stores for gifts
Hyundai Department Store COEX is connected: food hall on B1
Screenshot the floor map; shop codes confuse everyone

stops.note: The giant 3D “wave” screen outside COEX. Stand on the plaza opposite, not underneath.
do: The wave loop plays every few minutes between ads

stops.note: American-style pizza and craft beer; opens 13:00, so walk in and grab the big table.
do: Order 3 larges for 5: garlic white (₩39,000), combination (₩43,000), pepperoni (₩29,000)
Craft beer on tap; sports on the big screens

stops.note: Free five-floor car-tech showroom: concept cars, Genesis and N performance models, design exhibits.
do: Start at the top floor and walk down
Sit in the cars; staff speak English

stops.note: Gentle Monster’s surreal flagship: a giant robotic sculpture, eyewear floors, Tamburins perfume on 4F.
do: 1F: the moving robot installation
4F: try Tamburins hand creams and scents
B1 Nudake: the “black croissant” and cakes, like art objects (≈₩12k each)

stops.note: Perfect 5.0 massage spot (148 reviews). Foot soak, then full-body massage in private rooms.
do: Book 5 × Relief Special (80 min, ₩87,000) on Naver Reservation or by phone
Reservation-only, no walk-ins

legs.to: The Hanoi Foot & Body, Cheongdam Le Ciel

stops.note: New York dry-aged steakhouse; the porterhouse is the reason to come.
do: For 5: 1.5 kg porterhouse + creamed spinach + German potatoes + a salad
Porterhouse is ₩370,000 per kg; ask the server to size it for five
Book a table for 5 on CatchTable

legs.from: The Hanoi Foot & Body, Cheongdam Le Ciel

stops.note: One of Asia’s 50 Best Bars: relaxed lounge, sustainable cocktails and friendly English-speaking staff.
do: Try the Jeju Garibaldi (hallabong + house gin)
Cocktails ≈₩25,000; non-alcoholic sodas made in-house
Opens 18:30 on Mondays; book a table for 5

tips: Cheaper steak: Stubborn (Gangnam) at ≈₩40–75k per person, or Jang Steakhouse (hanwoo) nearby in Apgujeong.
Tired by mid-afternoon? Swap the Motorstudio for a Dolby Cinema film at Megabox COEX (Hollywood films in English).
Closed today (Monday): Leeum, D Museum, Centre Pompidou, Amorepacific museum. That’s why the art is on Tuesday.

title: Seongsu & Hannam
summary: Blue Bottle in Seongsu, deer in Seoul Forest, an immersive art museum, Italian-Korean lunch, last-chance K-beauty shopping, Leeum’s landmark architecture, a photo exhibition and vinyl library, then fresh pasta and a rooftop farewell drink.

stops.note: Blue Bottle’s Seoul flagship in an old red-brick building. Quiet before 10:00.
do: Try the NOLA iced coffee and a Liège waffle

stops.note: Flat paths, ginkgo avenue and the deer enclosure. An easy morning stroll.
do: Head for the sika deer enclosure (Seongsu side)
Butterfly garden open until 16:30

stops.note: An immersive walk-through contemporary art show, very photogenic. Opens 11:00.
do: Buy tickets online (₩18,000 adult) to skip the queue
Don’t miss the rooftop terrace view

stops.note: Tiny neighbourhood trattoria rated 5.0: Italian with a Korean twist.
do: Share: skirt steak with potato purée (₩37,000), pork & jeyuk cream risotto (₩20,000), spicy octopus pasta (₩19,000)
Small room: call ahead for 5; backup is Parco (wood-fired pizza, everything ₩20,800) near Seoul Forest

stops.note: Raw-concrete fragrance flagship with a new art installation each season.
do: Free testers: hand creams and perfumes make easy gifts (₩35–45k)

stops.note: Olive Young’s biggest K-beauty store: last-chance shopping with instant tax-free prices.
do: Bring passports: tax is removed at the till
Masks, sunscreen and skincare gifts; staff help with recommendations
Free photo booth on 1F

stops.note: Three landmark buildings by Botta, Nouvel and Koolhaas, plus Anish Kapoor’s mirrors and Louise Bourgeois’s spider.
do: Taxi from Seongsu (≈15 min, ≈₩15k in a Venti)
Book online: “Into Other Spaces” ₩18,000; M2 contemporary wing
Skip the traditional ceramics floors (history)
Closes 18:00; last entry 17:30

stops.note: Sung Ryul’s “Summer-Like Us”: dreamy large-format photography, self-paced.
do: Ticket sales stop at 18:00; ₩20,000 adult
Under the Gourmet494 food hall

stops.note: Cool vinyl complex: the Vinyl & Plastic record shop and listening tables are open to everyone.
do: Pick any LP and play it at a listening station
The library upstairs is members-only; the shop floor is free

legs.to: Hyundai Card Music Library & Vinyl & Plastic

stops.note: Fresh-pasta osteria for the farewell dinner.
do: Share: 1++ beef carpaccio (₩29,000), white-ragù tajarin, shrimp ravioli (₩28–32k), Orzo salad (₩15,000)
Order 5–6 plates for the table plus a bottle of wine

legs.from: Hyundai Card Music Library & Vinyl & Plastic

stops.note: The Mondrian’s indoor-outdoor rooftop. Tuesdays are relaxed, with city lights all around.
do: Reserve a terrace table on CatchTable
Single malts and signature cocktails ≈₩28–35k

tips: Wednesday: pack tonight. Olive Young and Musinsa (next door) tax refunds are instant, so there’s nothing to claim at the airport.
Rather have beer than art? Swap Ground Seesaw for Seoul Brewery Seongsu (flights of house beer, wood-fired pizza).
Seongsu → Hannam is quickest by Venti/TADA (≈15 min).
